alternatives.argument: Tong’s author-hosted HTML §4.2, lines 101–110, states that endpoint energy change has separate work and heat-transfer contributions, defines heat as a transfer process rather than stored state energy, and permits processes whose intermediate evolution is not maintained in equilibrium. OpenStax §§3.2–3.3 independently treats heat and work as process transfers and gives the endpoint first-law balance. The local item adopts typed protocol fields and imposes no path regularity as a definition; these source statements support its physical distinctions without claiming a theorem about every microscopic path.

Tong’s author-hosted HTML §4.2, lines 98–107, explicitly writes ΔE=Q+W with work done on an isolated system and heat as energy transferred to the system; it also states that neither heat nor work is a state function. OpenStax §3.3 independently states the equivalent ΔU=Q−W_by convention with Q into the system. These source statements support the adopted balance and sign convention. They do not prove the physical postulate from mechanics or from experiments; the item explicitly records it as an adopted conditional model law and excludes matter and omitted-energy changes.
